relations.myth: The Devil instructs meigas in harmful magic
relations.note: Some accused meigas allegedly learned magical powers from the Devil.

relations.myth: A meiga gains powers through a diabolical pact
relations.note: Demonological accusations claimed meigas obtained powers by pacts with the Devil.

relations.myth: Meigas meet the Devil during nocturnal assemblies
relations.note: Later folklore places flying or transformed meigas at gatherings with the Devil.

relations.myth: Alleged sexual relations with the Devil
relations.note: Coerced confessions and demonological accusations sometimes alleged sexual relations with the Devil.

relations.myth: Christ's baptism is invoked in a healing formula
relations.note: Ana de Castro invoked Christ's baptism in the Jordan while performing a cure.

relations.myth: Mary is invoked in cures against meigallo
relations.note: Healing formulas invoke Mary, while O Corpiño pilgrims seek her intercession against meigallo.

relations.myth: Peter accompanies Christ in a healing formula
relations.note: Ana de Castro's formula describes Saint Peter holding Christ by the hand.

relations.myth: John appears in a formula against magical affliction
relations.note: Saint John appears in Ana de Castro's cure and later protective seasonal folklore.

relations.myth: Queimada conjuration calls for Satan's expulsion
relations.note: The revised queimada text names Satan as an evil presence to expel.

relations.myth: Queimada conjuration calls for Beelzebub's expulsion
relations.note: The revised queimada text names Beelzebub among evil presences to expel.

relations.myth: Meigas and Santa Compaña share supernatural imagery
relations.note: They appear together in modern imagery and the queimada text without a stable narrative relation.
